stages.title: Connect to every app
stages.blurb: Admin connects an app once. A connector reads it with the least access that works, at the app's own pace, and turns what it finds into one shared shape.

stages.title: Catch every change
stages.blurb: Each change reaches the brain by the cheapest reliable path: a push when the app offers one, a cursor poll otherwise, and a slow full sweep to catch what both missed.

stages.title: The pointer index
stages.blurb: The brain keeps pointers, facts about each document, access lists and search vectors. Document bodies are read on demand and thrown away after the vectors are made.

stages.title: Permissions follow the user
stages.blurb: Every result is checked against the access list the source app holds. The index narrows the search by permission first; for the final few results the app is asked again.

stages.title: Answer a question
stages.blurb: A question is planned, routed to the index or to the live app, ranked, checked against the user's permissions, read fresh, and answered with citations.

stages.title: Interfaces for LLMs and agents
stages.blurb: Any model or agent can ask the brain through MCP or a plain API, under its own identity, and gets results that say where they came from and how current they are.

stages.title: Connect to AI clients
stages.blurb: One remote MCP server reaches Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and Gemini. Each client signs the user in, sees a small set of tools, and gets the answer under its own limits.

stages.title: Freshness, quality and cost
stages.blurb: The index is measured against the apps it points at: how late it is, what it misses, whether it leaks, and what each question and document costs.

stages.title: Privacy, deletion and tenant safety
stages.blurb: What the brain keeps is small and sensitive. It must forget when the app forgets, keep tenants apart, honour each app's terms and stop on command.

stages.title: Platform parts the brain owns
stages.blurb: The brain is its own product. It runs these parts itself and picks standard tools for each, so it needs no host system.

stages.title: Personal, team and company zones
stages.blurb: Admin access sees what the company shares. Per-user access sees what only one person can. Every pointer is tagged with a zone from its source, and personal data stays with its owner.

stages.title: Capture AI chats and work activity
stages.blurb: A small app on each laptop and the vendor admin feeds bring in AI chats and work activity as personal-zone records, with the owner in control.

stages.title: Credential and agent security
stages.blurb: Tokens never reach an agent. Only the connector runtime opens them. Everything an agent reads is scanned and scoped, and an agent cannot ask for a secret.

stages.title: Record work and update tools
stages.blurb: A separate action agent reads context from the brain and proposes updates to Jira and similar tools. It writes with the user's own token after the user confirms.

so_admin.label: Workspace admin
so_admin.pin: admin consent screen with a scope diff the admin approves before any token is issued

so_oauth.label: Token vault
so_oauth.pin: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code grant with refresh tokens, wrapped by a KMS key per tenant (RFC 6749)

so_svc.label: App-only access
so_svc.pin: admin-consented app-only access (domain-wide delegation, application permissions), read-only scopes from a catalog

so_obo.label: On-behalf-of exchange
so_obo.pin: OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693) and the Microsoft on-behalf-of flow: trade the user's brain token for a short-lived app token

so_sdk.label: Connector SDK
so_sdk.pin: declarative manifest (auth, streams, pagination, incremental cursor, ACL mapping) with a code hook, as in Airbyte low-code connectors

so_cap.label: Capability probe
so_cap.pin: per-app capability descriptor {webhook, delta, list, search, acl_api, rate}; the cheapest freshness path that works is chosen

so_rate.label: Rate-limit budgeter
so_rate.pin: hierarchical token bucket per (tenant, app, endpoint) that honours Retry-After and shares a fair queue between tenants

so_mcp.label: MCP bridge
so_mcp.sub: Apps that ship an MCP server
so_mcp.pin: Model Context Protocol client that calls an app's own MCP server for live read and search when no native connector exists

so_norm.label: Schema normaliser
so_norm.pin: map each app object to a Document, Message, Principal or Event envelope with a stable URI, a version and a content hash

so_apps.label: Company apps
so_apps.sub: Slack, Drive, 365, Notion, Jira, GitHub, CRM
so_apps.pin: vendor REST, GraphQL and webhook APIs; the system of record stays here

ch_hook.label: Webhook receiver
ch_hook.pin: HMAC signature check, replay window, acknowledge in under 200 ms, enqueue the event and do no work inline

ch_delta.label: Delta poller
ch_delta.pin: per-stream change cursor (Microsoft Graph delta link, Drive changes page token), persisted and resumable

ch_cdc.label: Database change tail
ch_cdc.pin: log-based change data capture (Debezium style) for sources that expose a transaction log

ch_sweep.label: Reconciliation sweep
ch_sweep.pin: slow full listing compared against a per-folder hash digest, so only differing subtrees are re-read

ch_sched.label: Adaptive scheduler
ch_sched.pin: poll interval from an EWMA of the observed change rate, clamped between 30 s and 6 h and capped by the rate budget

ch_bus.label: Change event log
ch_bus.pin: partitioned append-only log keyed by tenant and document, at-least-once delivery

ch_dedupe.label: Idempotency and ordering
ch_dedupe.pin: compare-and-set on (doc_id, source_version): apply only when the version is newer than the stored one

ch_wf.label: Durable sync workflow
ch_wf.sub: Retry, resume, never lose a cursor
ch_wf.pin: durable-execution workflow (Temporal style) with resumable cursors, bounded retries and per-source concurrency

ch_fill.label: Backfill crawler
ch_fill.pin: priority-ordered initial crawl (recent, shared and popular first) so search works before the crawl ends

ch_tomb.label: Tombstone propagation
ch_tomb.pin: a delete or permission removal soft-deletes the pointer at once and queues a purge of everything derived from it

ch_cursor.label: Cursor store
ch_cursor.pin: transactional store of {stream, cursor, watermark} written in the same transaction as the events it covers

ch_dlq.label: Dead-letter queue
ch_dlq.sub: Parked failures with a replay tool
ch_dlq.pin: parked events with an error class, retry history and a one-click replay

ix_ptr.label: Pointer registry
ix_ptr.sub: One row per object, no body
ix_ptr.pin: row {uri, app, source_id, version, content_hash, title, owner, times, acl_ref, vector_ids}; the body is never written

ix_meta.label: Filter attributes
ix_meta.pin: columnar attributes the search engine filters on before it scores

ix_ent.label: Entity resolver
ix_ent.sub: Same person or project across apps
ix_ent.pin: blocking plus pairwise match scoring (Fellegi-Sunter style) with a merge audit trail

ix_link.label: Relationship graph
ix_link.pin: property graph of document-to-document, person-to-document and document-to-entity edges, stored as adjacency lists

ix_fresh.label: Freshness stamp
ix_fresh.pin: each pointer carries source_version and last_verified; staleness is now minus last_verified

ix_def.label: Business definitions
ix_def.pin: versioned semantic contract {term, definition, owner, valid_from, valid_to, source_uri}; a query that uses a term is rewritten to the definition in force on the question date

ix_att.label: Claim and attestation record
ix_att.pin: each claim holds one meaning; each attestation holds a locator, content hash, author, observed time and validity window, and strength is computed when read

ix_fetch.label: Transient fetcher
ix_fetch.sub: Read the body, keep it in memory
ix_fetch.pin: fetch through the connector by pointer; the body lives in memory only and is dropped after derivation

ix_ext.label: Text extractor
ix_ext.pin: format-specific extraction that keeps headings, tables and message turns

ix_chunk.label: Structure-aware chunker
ix_chunk.sub: Cut on meaning, not on count
ix_chunk.pin: split on headings, message turns and function bounds with a 256 to 512 token target and small overlap

ix_ctx.label: Context line writer
ix_ctx.sub: One sentence of context per chunk
ix_ctx.pin: contextual retrieval: a cheap model writes a short situating line prepended to the chunk before embedding, cached by content hash

ix_pii.label: Sensitivity classifier
ix_pii.pin: detector for secrets and personal data that drops or masks them before embedding and sets a sensitivity label

ix_embed.label: Embedding service
ix_embed.pin: dense embedding through the model gateway, batched, with the model id stored on every vector

ix_cat.label: Artifact catalog
ix_cat.sub: What kind of thing each pointer is
ix_cat.pin: typed catalog row per pointer {artifact_type, entities[], period, owner_team, summary_ref}, built from metadata and the first screen of text; search narrows to candidate ids here before any vector is touched

ix_lex.label: Lexical index
ix_lex.pin: BM25 inverted index with block-max WAND pruning, sharded by tenant

ix_vec.label: Vector index
ix_vec.pin: approximate nearest-neighbour index (HNSW or DiskANN) with int8 or binary quantisation, partitioned by tenant, filter-aware

ix_snip.label: Snippet cache
ix_snip.sub: Short excerpt for ranking and preview
ix_snip.pin: excerpt capped at 300 characters, encrypted, with a time to live

ix_gc.label: Index garbage collector
ix_gc.pin: epoch-based collection of vectors and postings whose pointer is tombstoned

ix_reidx.label: Re-embed migrator
ix_reidx.pin: blue-green index versions: build the new one beside the old, dual-write, cut over, retire

ac_scim.label: Directory sync
ac_scim.pin: SCIM 2.0 and identity-provider feeds for users, groups and offboarding events

ac_id.label: Identity mapper
ac_id.pin: map each app's user id to one company principal by verified email, SCIM id and IdP subject

ac_src.label: ACL fetcher
ac_src.pin: read each object's sharing list (Drive permissions, SharePoint, Slack channel members, Jira project roles)

ac_grp.label: Group expander
ac_grp.pin: cycle-safe nested group flattening with versioned membership snapshots and lazy expansion for very large groups

ac_store.label: Access list store
ac_store.pin: document id to a set of principal and group ids, stored apart from content so it can change on its own

ac_filter.label: Filter compiler
ac_filter.sub: Search only what you may see
ac_filter.pin: user to principal set to a pre-filter pushed into lexical and vector search; never filter after ranking alone

ac_live.label: Live permission recheck
ac_live.sub: Ask the app again for the top results
ac_live.pin: verify the top-k with the source app using the user's token before display; fail closed

ac_neg.label: Revocation fast path
ac_neg.sub: Lost access takes effect in seconds
ac_neg.pin: revoked-principal cache with push invalidation and a seconds-long time to live

ac_audit.label: Access audit log
ac_audit.sub: Who saw which object, under which list
ac_audit.pin: append-only record of principal, query, objects shown, ACL version and any source recheck

ac_gate.label: Ownership gate
ac_gate.sub: Hard check after retrieval, before the model
ac_gate.pin: every retrieved chunk carries owner and zone; a chunk whose owner or zone is not in the caller's allowed set is dropped by code, not by a prompt, and each drop is counted

ac_lin.label: Derived-object access
ac_lin.sub: A note is as private as its sources
ac_lin.pin: each stored card or note keeps a derived_from list; visibility is the intersection of the asker's rights on every source, rechecked lazily after a policy change

qr_id.label: Principal resolver
qr_id.pin: resolve the caller to a user principal, an optional agent id and a scope

qr_rw.label: Query planner
qr_rw.pin: a small model rewrites, decomposes and extracts entities; it never sees data, only the question

qr_route.label: Source router
qr_route.pin: cost-based choice per sub-question from freshness need, app capability and remaining rate budget

qr_cache.label: Result cache
qr_cache.pin: cache keyed by query and principal set, invalidated by change events

qr_scope.label: Candidate scoper
qr_scope.sub: Narrow to a few hundred ids first
qr_scope.pin: catalog and metadata filters produce a candidate id set (target under 500) that the lexical and vector search then rank inside, with the permission filter applied to the same set

qr_rev.label: Plan reviser
qr_rev.sub: Diagnose a bad step and change the plan
qr_rev.pin: after each step a small model checks the result against the sub-question, names the failure (empty, off-topic, wrong source, stale) and revises the next step, at most 3 revisions

qr_hyb.label: Hybrid retrieval
qr_hyb.pin: BM25 and dense nearest neighbours merged with reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60)

qr_graph.label: Graph expansion
qr_graph.pin: personalised PageRank over the relationship graph from the entities in the question

qr_live.label: Live federated search
qr_live.pin: fan-out to app search APIs or MCP tools with the user's token, 1.5 s deadline, merged by rank fusion

qr_rerank.label: Cross-encoder reranker
qr_rerank.pin: cross-encoder over the top 100 with recency and authority features

qr_hyd.label: Hydrator
qr_hyd.pin: fetch current text for the chosen pointers, validate by ETag, recheck access

qr_loop.label: Raw-record search loop
qr_loop.sub: Agent searches the records, step by step
qr_loop.pin: agentic loop with chat-native controls (grep by term, filter by channel, actor and time, read around a hit) over permitted raw records, capped at 8 steps and a token budget

qr_pack.label: Context packer
qr_pack.sub: Fit the best into the budget
qr_pack.pin: token-budgeted selection with maximal marginal relevance and ordering that fights the lost-in-the-middle effect

qr_inj.label: Injection quarantine
qr_inj.pin: retrieved text is wrapped as untrusted data; an instruction detector flags it and tool calls stay off in this context

qr_ans.label: Answer generator
qr_ans.pin: model call through the gateway with a cite-or-abstain instruction

qr_cite.label: Citation verifier
qr_cite.pin: check each claim span against its cited passage and drop what the passage does not support

qr_stamp.label: Freshness stamp
qr_stamp.sub: Say how current the answer is
qr_stamp.pin: attach source version and read time to every citation

qr_life.label: Evidence lifecycle check
qr_life.pin: each passage is labelled current, superseded or contradicted from version and link edges; set questions are checked for completeness and negations route to an absence check

ll_mcp.label: Brain MCP server
ll_mcp.pin: Model Context Protocol server over streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1; tools search, fetch, list_sources, who_knows

ll_api.label: REST and SDK
ll_api.sub: For code that is not an agent
ll_api.pin: REST with an OpenAPI description, idempotency keys, cursor pagination and generated SDKs

ll_schema.label: Tool contract
ll_schema.pin: tool names, descriptions and argument schemas tuned against a tool-use eval, with token-lean responses

ll_fmt.label: Result envelope
ll_fmt.pin: result {id, title, uri, snippet, score, source_app, version, retrieved_at, permission_checked_at}

ll_browse.label: Browsable knowledge files
ll_browse.sub: Agent reads index.md, then opens one file
ll_browse.pin: a generated tree of index.md and SKILL.md files with frontmatter {title, owner, updated, scope, open_with}, served per user so an agent lists, reads and follows links like a file system

ll_agent.label: Agent identity and scope
ll_agent.sub: Its own name, narrower than its owner
ll_agent.pin: per-agent principal with a named owner and a token scoped to no more than the owner may see

ll_quota.label: Quota and fairness
ll_quota.pin: token bucket per agent and tenant with the cost of each call metered

ll_sub.label: Change subscription
ll_sub.sub: Wake an agent when something changes
ll_sub.pin: agents subscribe to entity or topic change events and receive pushes

ll_ro.label: Read-only guard
ll_ro.sub: The brain does not write to apps
ll_ro.pin: the brain exposes no write tool; actions go through the action layer under policy

ll_delta.label: Change detector
ll_delta.pin: per user and per watched entity, diff the pointer and relationship changes since the last cursor, grouped by entity and kept as {entity, change, uri, at}

ll_score.label: Relevance scorer
ll_score.sub: Does this change matter to this person?
ll_score.pin: score = w1*role_match + w2*recency + w3*link_distance + w4*past_clicks, thresholded per user; only permitted changes are scored

ll_note.label: Notification writer
ll_note.pin: a small model turns the top deltas into a short notice with citations, one notice per entity per day, with a snooze and a never-again control

cl_meta.label: Login discovery
cl_meta.sub: Client finds the login server itself
cl_meta.pin: RFC 9728 protected resource metadata plus RFC 8414 server metadata, so a client learns where to sign in from a 401 reply

cl_reg.label: Client registration
cl_reg.pin: client ID metadata documents first, dynamic client registration as fallback, and a static pre-registered client for hosts that need one

cl_aud.label: Token audience check
cl_aud.sub: Token made for this server only
cl_aud.pin: PKCE S256, RFC 8707 resource indicator checked as the token audience, and RFC 9207 issuer in the redirect

cl_consent.label: Connect-an-app prompt
cl_consent.sub: Ask the user to link a source
cl_consent.pin: URL-mode elicitation that sends the user to the brain's own consent page when a source app is not linked yet

cl_search.label: Search and fetch pair
cl_search.pin: two tools named search and fetch that return {id, title, text, url}, as ChatGPT deep research and company knowledge expect

cl_budget.label: Tool and output budget
cl_budget.pin: few tools with exact names, results under 25,000 tokens, a result-size hint on large tools, server instructions under 4,096 characters

cl_dist.label: Org rollout configs
cl_dist.pin: generated managed config per client: managed-mcp.json, Claude.ai org connector, Copilot policy, Windsurf allowlist, Codex requirement, ChatGPT admin app

cl_plugin.label: Skill and context snippets
cl_plugin.sub: Tell agents when to ask the brain
cl_plugin.pin: a Claude plugin with a skill, plus CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md snippets that name the brain tools and when to call them

cl_net.label: Public endpoint
cl_net.pin: public HTTPS URL with an allowlist of vendor IP ranges, and a private registry instead of the public MCP registry

cl_tasks.label: Slow query tasks
cl_tasks.pin: the MCP Tasks extension for slow multi-source queries, with polling and a cancel call

op_lag.label: Freshness lag monitor
op_lag.pin: lag is now minus source modified time, tracked as p95 per source against a stated target

op_audit.label: Sampling audit
op_audit.sub: Check a sample against the app
op_audit.pin: random pointers checked against the live app for existence, version and access, with a capture-recapture coverage estimate

op_cov.label: Coverage estimator
op_cov.pin: compare indexed object counts with cheap count calls to the app

op_health.label: Connector health
op_health.pin: error budget and circuit breaker that pauses a failing connector and opens a repair task

op_beat.label: Silent-failure heartbeat
op_beat.sub: A quiet source is not a healthy source
op_beat.pin: each connector must emit a heartbeat and a count of objects seen; no heartbeat, or zero new objects against an expected rate, raises a health alarm and forces a sweep

op_eval.label: Retrieval evaluation
op_eval.pin: recall at k, nDCG at 10 and MRR on a per-tenant golden set, run on every index change

op_leak.label: Permission leak test
op_leak.pin: synthetic users with known access lists; any unauthorised hit fails the release

op_cost.label: Cost meter
op_cost.pin: cost per document indexed and per query from embedding, storage and app API calls

op_trace.label: Query trace store
op_trace.pin: full trace of plan, retrieve, live calls and rerank, replayable against a past index version

op_attr.label: Failure attributor
op_attr.sub: Which stage caused the bad answer?
op_attr.pin: given a failed trace, a model assigns the failure to one stage (route, retrieve, rank, permission, compose) with evidence, and the cause is counted per week

op_ver.label: Versioned pipeline release
op_ver.sub: Prompts, rules and indexes ship as versions
op_ver.pin: planner prompts, chunk rules, rerank weights and thresholds are versioned artifacts; a candidate version must beat the current one on the golden set under a judge before it goes live, and rolls back in one call

gv_erase.label: Erasure propagation
gv_erase.sub: Delete in the app, gone here
gv_erase.pin: a source delete becomes a tombstone that purges pointers, vectors, snippets, caches and traces within a stated time, with a receipt

gv_kms.label: Tenant keys and region
gv_kms.pin: per-tenant envelope encryption with an optional customer-held key and region pinning

gv_inv.label: Embedding protection
gv_inv.pin: treat embeddings as sensitive data: encrypted at rest, never exported, rotated per tenant

gv_tenant.label: Tenant isolation
gv_tenant.pin: tenant id in every key and shard, with row-level policy as a second check

gv_tos.label: Vendor terms registry
gv_tos.sub: What each app lets us keep
gv_tos.pin: per-app allowed use (cache time, training ban, rate) enforced by configuration

gv_line.label: Store-or-point rule
gv_line.sub: What the brain may keep, and what it only points to
gv_line.pin: a table of what may be stored per object class: pointers, filters and a 300-character excerpt by default; derived notes only with a source list and an owner

gv_kill.label: Pause and purge switch
gv_kill.sub: Stop one connector or one tenant
gv_kill.pin: per-connector and per-tenant kill switch that stops sync and purges derived data

pl_gw.label: LLM gateway
pl_gw.pin: one gateway such as LiteLLM routes by cost and quality, meters spend per team and redacts personal data

pl_idp.label: Identity and audit
pl_idp.pin: an OpenID Connect provider for users and agents, plus a hash-chained audit table nobody can edit

pl_pol.label: Policy engine
pl_pol.pin: versioned rule files in OPA or Cedar, checked before any agent action

pl_mem.label: Lessons store
pl_mem.pin: a per-tenant table of corrections and preferences, linked to the eval tests that guard them

pl_obs.label: Traces and eval gates
pl_obs.pin: OpenTelemetry traces and a CI eval suite that blocks a release, plus an incident log

zn_tag.label: Zone tagger
zn_tag.pin: zone is read from the source's own sharing setting (private channel, DM, My Drive, shared drive), never guessed by a model

zn_scope.label: Owner filter
zn_scope.sub: Personal rows match their owner only
zn_scope.pin: owner id is a mandatory filter term inside the ANN and BM25 query for every personal-zone row, checked again at hydrate

zn_key.label: Per-user key
zn_key.sub: Personal data under the owner's key
zn_key.pin: envelope encryption with one data key per user wrapped by the tenant KMS key; deleting the user key crypto-shreds their zone

zn_promote.label: Promotion gate
zn_promote.sub: Personal to team only with consent
zn_promote.pin: an item leaves the personal zone only when the source sharing changes or the owner confirms in a prompt; a model never promotes

zn_taint.label: Derived-data taint
zn_taint.pin: every cache entry, entity, lesson and trace carries the highest zone of its inputs, and a company-level store rejects a personal taint

zn_review.label: Preview and correct
zn_review.sub: Owner sees and edits before sharing
zn_review.pin: before any case or chat excerpt leaves the personal zone the owner gets a preview with the exact text, can edit or strike lines, and approves; the approval record is kept

cr_mode.label: Credential mode policy
cr_mode.sub: Admin crawl, user link, or both
cr_mode.pin: per connector and per zone mode table: company zone via app-only grant, personal zone via the user's own grant, strict mode forces user grant for all

cr_link.label: One-time user link
cr_link.sub: Sign in once, link without a second login
cr_link.pin: the user signs in once through company single sign-on, and linking an app reuses that session; only apps with no federation show a consent page

cr_union.label: Merged view
cr_union.sub: Admin view plus the user's own view
cr_union.pin: results from the admin-crawled index and the user-linked index are merged by uri, and the stricter ACL wins on a conflict

cr_gap.label: Coverage gap report
cr_gap.sub: What the admin crawl cannot see
cr_gap.pin: per source, count objects the app-only grant cannot list and prompt the owner to link, using a probe of the user's own listing

cp_daemon.label: Local daemon
cp_daemon.pin: a signed background process that watches an allowlist of session folders and posts new turns over an outbound-only TLS channel

cp_hook.label: Session hook reader
cp_hook.pin: session-end and stop hooks plus a tail of the local JSONL transcript files, resuming from a byte offset per file

cp_redact.label: On-device redaction
cp_redact.pin: pattern and entropy secret scan (gitleaks style) plus personal-data masking, run before any byte leaves the laptop

cp_vault.label: Keychain and consent
cp_vault.sub: Owns the credentials, shows a pause button
cp_vault.pin: tokens stay in the operating system keychain, only the daemon reads them, and a visible pause switch stops capture at once

cp_mdm.label: Rollout and update
cp_mdm.pin: a signed and notarised installer pushed by device management with a pinned auto-update channel and a remote disable

cf_claude.label: Claude compliance feed
cf_claude.pin: Anthropic compliance API pulled on a schedule with a compliance access key, for web and desktop chats

cf_openai.label: ChatGPT compliance feed
cf_openai.pin: OpenAI compliance logs pulled in time windows as JSONL, scoped by workspace

cf_vault.label: Other chat exports
cf_vault.pin: Google Vault export and Microsoft Purview or Graph interaction records, pulled by the same scheduled runner

cf_norm.label: Chat normaliser
cf_norm.pin: each turn becomes a Message envelope {uri, owner, tool, session, turn, time, content_hash} stamped zone personal

cf_del.label: Delete reconciler
cf_del.pin: each export or hook run is diffed against the pointer set and any turn no longer reported becomes a tombstone

cf_struct.label: Chat views
cf_struct.sub: By channel, by person, by artifact
cf_struct.pin: each Message is attached to three views, channel thread, actor timeline and artifact link, so a search can open the view that fits the question

cp_exp.label: Experience distiller
cp_exp.sub: Turn a finished task into a case
cp_exp.pin: a model reads the owner's session and writes a case with six elements {situation, goal, actions, decision rule, outcome, caveat}, always as a draft the owner reviews

cp_probe.label: Claim probe
cp_probe.sub: Check the card against the live source
cp_probe.pin: before review, read-only calls to the live app test each card claim for support, scope and current validity, using the contributor's own permissions

cp_dup.label: Duplicate and conflict check
cp_dup.sub: Is this case already on a shelf?
cp_dup.pin: compare the draft with the five nearest cards after a tag prefilter, then mark it new, a duplicate, a clarification or a conflict

cp_trust.label: Card evidence tier
cp_trust.pin: a card starts as a prediction from one case, becomes core after three independent cases agree, and an anchor after ten review cycles without contradiction

cp_lib.label: Case libraries
cp_lib.pin: six libraries (situation, action, decision rule, failure, tool, glossary) holding approved cases as pointers to the owner's source, retrieved by situation similarity

sc_runtime.label: Token boundary
sc_runtime.pin: tokens are decrypted only inside the connector runtime process, which has no inbound tool surface and no model access

sc_split.label: Separate admin and user keys
sc_split.sub: One breach does not reach both
sc_split.pin: admin app-only tokens and per-user tokens sit under different KMS keys and different roles, and neither role can read the other

sc_noconf.label: No credential tools
sc_noconf.sub: Nothing to ask for a secret
sc_noconf.pin: the tool list has no tool that returns, lists or edits a credential or connector setting; a test fails the build if one appears

sc_scan.label: Secret scan on index and output
sc_scan.pin: gitleaks style rules and entropy checks on every chunk before indexing and on every answer before it leaves

sc_scope.label: Agent scope and trifecta guard
sc_scope.pin: per-agent scope set checked by the policy engine, and no agent holds private data, untrusted input and an outbound channel at once

sc_egress.label: Egress allowlist
sc_egress.pin: outbound destinations limited to an allowlist and rendered links and images stripped from answers

ag_collect.label: Activity collector
ag_collect.pin: reads the user's own personal-zone sessions and tool events for a day window, scoped by the owner filter

ag_plan.label: Update planner
ag_plan.pin: a model proposes {tool, issue, change, evidence} items from collected activity and brain context, never a write

ag_gate.label: Confirmation gate
ag_gate.pin: each proposed write waits for the owner's approval by default, and a per-tool auto-approve list is opt-in

ag_write.label: Scoped writer
ag_write.sub: Writes with the user's own token
ag_write.pin: one write call per approved item through the user's own grant, idempotent by a client key, then logged

ag_priv.label: Quote guard
ag_priv.sub: Private chat never pasted in public
ag_priv.pin: any text copied from the personal zone into a company tool is paraphrased or blocked unless the owner confirms it
